title: Systems Manager Patch Compliance

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.71 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.71 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:ssm:compliance` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:ssm:compliance" ComplianceType="Patch"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.71_systems_manager_patch_co_71"
| sort -_time
description: Patch baselines reduce exploit exposure; instance-level compliance gaps show outdated AMIs or broken agents.
value: Detecting systems manager patch compliance early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Schedule `AWS-RunPatchBaseline` and ingest compliance association results. Dashboard by OU and environment tag. Alert when CRITICAL severity patches are non-compliant past SLA window.
visualization: Table (instance, missing count), Pie chart (compliant %), Bar chart (severity).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Updates.Updates
  where match(Updates.status, "(?i)non-?compliant|missing|failed|not.?installed")
  by Updates.dest Updates.app span=1d
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Updates: for `aws:ssm:compliance` and patch status mapped to CIM. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Patch waves not finished yet, instances powered off, and CAB exceptions you already published.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:ssm:compliance`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Schedule `AWS-RunPatchBaseline` and ingest compliance association results. Dashboard by OU and environment tag. Alert when CRITICAL severity patches are non-compliant past SLA window.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:ssm:compliance" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:ssm:compliance" ComplianceType="Patch"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.71_systems_manager_patch_co_71"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:ssm:compliance` in `index=aws` to detect systems manager patch compliance. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_71_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (instance, missing count), Pie chart (compliant %), Bar chart (severity)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of systems manager patch compliance so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
